L6@P1: The bias of the data shall be determined based on the relative accuracy (RA) test
L7@P1: data sets and the relative accuracy test audit (RATA) data sets for SOx pollutant
L8@P1: concentration monitors, fuel gas sulfur content monitors, flow monitors, and
L9@P1: emission rate measurement systems using the procedures outlined below.
L10@P1: 1. Calculate the mean of the difference using Equation 2-1 of 40 CFR, Part
L11@P1: 60, Appendix B, Performance Specification 2. To calculate bias for an
L12@P1: SOx pollutant concentration monitor, "d" shall, for each paired data point,
L13@P1: be the difference between the SOx concentration values (in ppmv)
L14@P1: obtained from the reference method and the monitor. To calculate bias for
L15@P1: a fuel gas sulfur content monitor, "d" shall, for each paired data point, be
L16@P1: the difference between the fuel gas sulfur concentration values (in ppmv)
L17@P1: obtained from the reference method and the -monitor. To calculate bias
L18@P1: for a flow monitor, "d" shall, for each paired data point, be the difference
L19@P1: between the flow rate values (in scfh) obtained from the reference method
L20@P1: and the monitor. To calculate bias for an emission rate measurement
L21@P1: system, "d" shall, for each paired data point, be the difference between the
L22@P1: emission rate values (in lb/hr) obtained from the reference method and the
L23@P1: monitoring system.
L24@P1: 2. Calculate the standard deviation, Sd, of the data set using Equation 2-2 of
L25@P1: 40 CFR, Part 60, Appendix B, Performance Specification 2.
L26@P1: 3. Calculate the confidence coefficient, cc, of the data set using Equation 2-3
L27@P1: of 40 CFR, Part 60, Appendix B, Performance Specification 2.
L28@P1: 4. The monitor passes the bias test if it meets either of the following criteria:
L29@P1: a. the absolute value of the mean difference is less than |cc|.
L30@P1: b. the absolute value of the mean difference is less than 1 ppmv.
L31@P1: 5. Alternatively, if the monitoring device fails to meet the bias test
L32@P1: requirement, the Facility Permit holder may choose to use the bias
L33@P1: adjustment procedure as follows:

L35@P1-2: correction will be applied. PROTOCOL FOR RULE 2011 January 7, 2005

L41@P2: B. Test Definitions, Performance Specifications and Test Procedures
L42@P2: This section explains in detail how each performance requirement is to be
L43@P2: conducted.
L44@P2-3: Low Level Calibration Error PROTOCOL FOR RULE 2012 January 7, 2005
L45@P3:  Rule 2012 - Att G - 2
L46@P3: The low level calibration error test is defined as challenging the CEMS
L47@P3: (from probe to monitor) with certified calibration gases (NO in N2) at
L48@P3: three levels in the 0-20 percent full scale span range. Since stable or
L49@P3: certifiable cylinder gas standards (e.g. Protocol 1 or NIST traceable) may
L50@P3: not be available at the concentrations required for this test, gas dilution
L51@P3: systems may be used, with District approval, if they are used according to
L52@P3: either District or EPA protocols for the verification of gas dilution systems
L53@P3: in the field. The CEMS high level calibration gas may be diluted for the
L54@P3: purpose of conducting the low level calibration error test.
L55@P3: 1. Performance Specifications
L56@P3: Introduce pollutant concentrations at approximately the 20
L57@P3: percent, 10 percent, and 5 percent of full scale span levels
L58@P3: through the normal CEMS calibration system. No low
L59@P3: level calibration error shall exceed 2.5 percent of full scale
L60@P3: span.
L61@P3: 2. Testing Procedures
L62@P3: a. Perform a standard zero/span check; if zero or span
L63@P3: check exceeds 2.5 percent full scale span, adjust
L64@P3: monitor and redo zero/span check.
L65@P3: b. After zero/span check allow the CEMS to sample
L66@P3: stack gas for at least 15 minutes.
L67@P3: c. Introduce any of the low level calibration error
L68@P3: standards through the CEMS calibration system.
L69@P3: d. Read the CEMS response to the calibration gas
L70@P3: starting no later than three system response times
L71@P3: after introducing the calibration gas; the CEMS
L72@P3: response shall be averaged for at least three
L73@P3: response times and for no longer than six response
L74@P3: times.
L75@P3: e. After the low level calibration error check allow the
L76@P3: CEMS to sample stack gas for at least 15 minutes.
L77@P3: f. Repeat steps c through e until all three low level
L78@P3: calibration error checks are complete.
L79@P3: g. Conduct post test calibration and zero checks.
L80@P3: Spike Recovery and Bias Factor Determinations
L81@P3: Spiking is defined as introducing know concentrations of the pollutant of
L82@P3: interest (gas standard to contain a mixture of NO and NO2 is
L83@P3: representative of the ratio of NO and NO2 in stack gas) and an appropriate
L84@P3: non-reactive, non-condensable and non-soluble tracer gas from a single
L85@P3-4: cylinder (Protocol 1 or NIST traceable to 2 percent analytical accuracy if PROTOCOL FOR RULE 2012 January 7, 2005
L86@P4:  Rule 2012 - Att G - 3
L87@P4: no Protocol 1 is available) near the probe and upstream of any sample
L88@P4: conditioning systems, at a flow rate not to exceed 10 percent of the total
L89@P4: sample gas flow rate. The purpose of the 10 percent limitation is to ensure
L90@P4: that the gas matrix (water, CO2, particulates, interferences) is essentially
L91@P4: the same as the stack gas alone. The tracer gas is monitored in real time
L92@P4: and the ratio of the monitored concentration to the certified concentration
L93@P4: in the cylinder is the dilution factor. The expected pollutant concentration
L94@P4: (dilution factor times the certified pollutant concentration in the cylinder)
L95@P4: is compared to the monitored pollutant concentration.
L96@P4: High Level Spike Recovery/Bias Factor Determination
L97@P4: The high level spike recovery/bias factor determination is used when it is
L98@P4: technologically not possible to certify the CEMS per the standard
L99@P4: RECLAIM requirements. The spiking facility/interface shall be a
L100@P4: permanently installed part of the CEMS sample acquisition system and
L101@P4: accessible to District staff as well as the Facility Permit holder.
L102@P4: 1. Performance Specifications
L103@P4: The CEMS shall demonstrate a RA </= 20 percent, where
L104@P4: the spike value is used in place of the reference method in
L105@P4: the normal RA calculation, as described below. The bias
L106@P4: factor, if applicable, shall also be determined according to
L107@P4: Attachment B.
L108@P4: 2. Testing Procedures
L109@P4: a. Spike the sample to the CEMS with a calibration
L110@P4: standard containing the pollutant of interest and CO
L111@P4: or other non-soluble, non-reacting alternative tracer
L112@P4: gas (alternative tracer gas) at a flow rate not to
L113@P4: exceed 10 percent of the CEMS sampling flow rate
L114@P4: and of such concentrations as to produce an
L115@P4: expected 40-80 percent of full scale span for the
L116@P4: pollutant of interest and a quantifiable concentration
L117@P4: of CO (or alternative tracer gas) that is at least a
L118@P4: factor of 10 higher than expected in the unspiked
L119@P4: stack gas. The calibration standards for both
L120@P4: pollutant of interest and CO (or alternative tracer
L121@P4: gas) must meet RECLAIM requirements specified
L122@P4: in Attachment A.
L123@P4: b. Monitor the CO (or alternative tracer gas) using an
L124@P4: appropriate continuous (or semi-continuous if
L125@P4: necessary) monitor meeting the requirements of
L126@P4: Method 100.1 and all data falling within the 10-95
L127@P4: percent full scale span, and preferably within 30-70
L128@P4: percent full scale span.
L129@P4: c. Alternate spiked sample gas and unspiked sample
L130@P4: gas for a total of nine runs of spiked sample gas and
L131@P4-5: ten runs of unspiked sample gas. Sampling times PROTOCOL FOR RULE 2012 January 7, 2005
L132@P5:  Rule 2012 - Att G - 4
L133@P5: should be sufficiently long to mitigate response time
L134@P5: and averaging effects.
L135@P5: d. For each run, the average CEMS reading must be
L136@P5: between 40 percent full scale span and 80 percent
L137@P5: full scale span. If not, adjust spiking as necessary
L138@P5: and continue runs; but expected spike must
L139@P5: represent at least 50 percent of the total pollutant
L140@P5: value read by the CEMS.
L141@P5: e. Calculate the spike recovery for both the pollutant
L142@P5: and the CO (or alternative tracer gas) for each run
L143@P5: by first averaging the pre- and post-spike values for
L144@P5: each run and subtracting that value from the spiked
L145@P5: value to yield nine values for recovered spikes.
L146@P5: f. Using the CO (or alternative tracer gas) spike
L147@P5: recovery values for each run and the certified CO
L148@P5: (or alternative tracer gas) concentration, calculate
L149@P5: the dilution ratio for each run. Multiply the certified
L150@P5: pollutant concentration by the dilution factor for
L151@P5: each run to determine the expected diluted pollutant
L152@P5: concentrations. Using the expected diluted
L153@P5: concentrations as the "reference method" value
L154@P5: calculate the Relative Accuracy as specified in
L155@P5: Appendix A. The RA shall be </= 20 percent.
L156@P5: Determine the bias factor, if applicable, according
L157@P5: to Attachment B.
L158@P5: Low Level Spike Recovery/Bias Factor Determination
L159@P5: The low level spike recovery/bias factor determination is used to
L160@P5: determine if a significant bias exists at concentrations near the 10 percent
L161@P5: full scale span level. The spiking facility/interface shall be a permanently
L162@P5: installed part of the CEMS sample acquisition system and accessible to
L163@P5: District staff as well as the Facility Permit holder.
L164@P5: 1. Performance Specifications
L165@P5: There are no pass/fail criteria with respect to the magnitude
L166@P5: of the percent relative accuracy. There are performance
L167@P5: criteria for the range of concentration on the CEMS and the
L168@P5: extent to which the spike must be greater than the
L169@P5: background pollutant level.
L170@P5: 2. Testing Procedures
L171@P5: a. Spike the sample to the CEMS with a calibration
L172@P5: standard containing the pollutant of interest and CO
L173@P5: or other non-soluble, non-reacting alternative tracer
L174@P5: gas (alternative tracer gas) at a flow rate not to
L175@P5: exceed 10 percent of the CEMS sampling flow rate
L176@P5-6: and of such concentrations as to produce an PROTOCOL FOR RULE 2012 January 7, 2005
L177@P6:  Rule 2012 - Att G - 5
L178@P6: expected 10-25 percent of full scale span for the
L179@P6: pollutant of interest and a quantifiable concentration
L180@P6: of CO (or alternative tracer gas) that is at least a
L181@P6: factor of 10 higher than expected in the unspiked
L182@P6: stack gas. The calibration standards for both
L183@P6: pollutant of interest and CO (or alternative tracer
L184@P6: gas) must meet RECLAIM requirements specified
L185@P6: in Appendix A.
L186@P6: b. Monitor the CO (or alternative tracer gas) using an
L187@P6: appropriate continuous (or semi-continuous if
L188@P6: necessary) monitor meeting the requirements of
L189@P6: Method 100.1 and all data falling within the 10-95
L190@P6: percent full scale span, and preferably within 30-70
L191@P6: percent full scale span.
L192@P6: c. Alternate spiked sample gas and unspiked sample
L193@P6: gas for a total of nine runs of spiked sample gas and
L194@P6: ten runs of unspiked sample gas. Sampling times
L195@P6: should be sufficiently long to mitigate response time
L196@P6: and averaging effects.
L197@P6: d. For each run, the average CEMS reading must be
L198@P6: below 25 percent full scale span and > 10 percent
L199@P6: full scale span. If not, adjust spiking as necessary
L200@P6: and continue runs; but expected spike must
L201@P6: represent at least 50 percent of the total pollutant
L202@P6: value read by the CEMS.
